product: Sorrelreach appointment assurance for nonprofit furniture collections

flaws.cause: The plan adds readiness confirmations while leaving vehicle loading and route sizes unchanged. The collection review shows donors were ready in nearly all failures, and a second-call test did not improve collection because the vans were full. Even complete use of the proposed messages leaves the established cause untouched.

evidence.what: Fifty-eight of 69 failures were full vehicles with ready donors; extra calls failed, while volume-based routing reached six percent failure.

flaws.changes_what_gets_built: Add item-volume-based route planning rather than more readiness confirmations as the collection repair.
flaws.fix: Use known furniture dimensions to keep booked loads within vehicle capacity and test completed collections against the current routes.

flaws.cause: The plan commits $210,000 irreversibly to an exclusive five-year service with no exit or assignment rights. A healthy monthly supplier already provides the required capabilities at the same integration effort, and there is no deadline or documented cost of staying with it that justifies the lock. This commitment remains unnecessary even if the product change is corrected.

evidence.what: Current service costs $310 monthly, has capacity and all needed functions; the five-year alternative adds no needed capability and has no return path.
The payment consumes most of the project envelope and would otherwise remain available for improvements.

flaws.changes_what_gets_built: Keep appointment messaging on a reversible monthly arrangement rather than purchase the exclusive long-term contract.
flaws.fix: Use the existing supplier for the bounded release; make any later long-term commitment conditional on a concrete benefit and negotiated exit terms.

notes: The ineffective service mechanism and the irreversible supplier purchase are separate decisions.
